deviation: The draft adds a broad Customer indemnity in favour of the Supplier (Customer Data, personal data consents, misuse), which the standard does not contain. It also drops the Supplier's mandatory indemnities for breach of law and gross negligence, leaving only a narrowed IP indemnity that is the "entire obligation" and has wide exclusions (Customer Data, specifications, combinations). The fallback to exclude gross negligence needs a cap of at least 2x annual fees, and the draft has no such cap or any compensating protection.
suggested_text: 12.1 The Supplier shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Customer and its affiliates, officers and employees from and against all third-party claims, and resulting losses, damages, costs and reasonable legal fees, arising from (a) the Supplier's breach of applicable law; (b) any allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe a third party's intellectual property rights; or (c) the Supplier's gross negligence. 12.2 If an infringement claim arises, the Supplier shall, in addition to its obligations under Section 12.1, at its own cost procure the right for the Customer to continue use, or modify or replace the Deliverable so it is non-infringing. The Supplier's obligations under Section 12.1 shall not apply to the extent a claim arises solely from the Customer's breach of this Agreement. 12.3 The indemnified party shall give prompt written notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party sole control of the defence and settlement, and provide reasonable assistance at the indemnifying party's cost. The indemnifying party shall not settle a claim imposing non-monetary obligations on the indemnified party without its consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. [Delete the Customer indemnity in the draft 12.1. If a Customer indemnity is unavoidable, limit it to third-party claims arising from the Customer's breach of law in providing Customer Data, and make it subject to the Customer's liability cap.]
